overview: Kerala Technology Startup Policy is implemented through Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), the nodal agency of the Government of Kerala for entrepreneurship development and incubation activities in Kerala, India. KSUM provides a comprehensive ecosystem of support including funding schemes, incubation, acceleration, market expansion, investor connections, and infrastructure to nurture startups across all stages of their journey. The policy aims to drive real change for startups by enabling access to markets, capital, partnerships, and growth opportunities, fostering a sustainable and inclusive startup ecosystem in the state.
objectives: Foster innovation and support entrepreneurs to drive sustainable economic growth
Create a highly sustainable startup ecosystem under the aegis of the Govt. of Kerala
Provide financial assistance through grants, loans, and reimbursements at various startup stages
Enable access to markets, capital, partnerships, and growth opportunities
Nurture creativity, experimentation, and entrepreneurial thinking among students via IEDC platforms
Support women and transgender-led startups through inclusive funding and ecosystem programs
Strengthen Kerala’s startup investment ecosystem via Fund of Funds and investor education initiatives
Facilitate structured collaboration between corporates and startups to accelerate innovation adoption
eligibility: Eligibility varies by scheme but generally requires startup incorporation as Private Limited Company, LLP, or OPC with active MCA status, a valid KSUM Unique ID, DPIIT recognition (where applicable), work on innovative technology-based products, and compliance with specific criteria such as revenue thresholds, shareholding by Indian promoters (≥51%), and absence of pending dues with government agencies. For women-focused schemes, women/transgender founders must hold ≥51% shareholding. Student innovators may apply without company incorporation but require IEDC association for fund disbursement.
benefits: KSUM offers financial support through grants (Idea Grant up to ₹3 lakhs, Productization Grant up to ₹7 lakhs, Market Acceleration Grant up to ₹10 lakhs, Scale-up Grant up to ₹15 lakhs, R&D Grant up to ₹30 lakhs, Women/Transgender Productization Grant up to ₹12 lakhs, NIDHI Prayas Grant up to ₹10 lakhs) and loans (Seed Fund up to ₹15 lakhs, Scaleup Seed Fund up to ₹25 lakhs, Women Soft Loan up to ₹15 lakhs, NIDHI Seed Support up to ₹1 crore). Non-financial benefits include incubation and acceleration programs, mentorship, infrastructure access (e.g., Super Fablab, Digital Hub), market expansion initiatives, investor connects (Investor Café, Pitch Days), business development support, and access to global platforms. Additional support includes patent reimbursement, technology transfer schemes, and specialized grants for social impact, agriculture, and creative economy sectors.
financial_support: Financial support is delivered through a mix of non-dilutive grants and soft loans. Grants are disbursed in milestone-based tranches (typically 50% first tranche, balance after progress review and utilization certificate). Loans are provided at 6% simple interest per annum with a 12-month moratorium and repayment in 36 monthly installments. The Fund of Funds channels capital into SEBI-registered AIFs that invest in Kerala-based startups. Specific schemes like NIDHI Seed Support offer funding from ₹25 lakhs to ₹1 crore for high-potential ventures. Disbursement is account payee cheque or bank transfer to company/IEDC accounts upon submission of required documents including incorporation details, PAN, KSUM Unique ID, bank details, and utilization certificates.
application_process: 1. Visit the KSUM website and navigate to the relevant scheme page. 2. Download guidelines and check eligibility. 3. Apply online during the call for applications via the KSUM portal. 4. Submit the application form with business profile and seed proposal. 5. Upload required documents (incorporation, PAN, KSUM Unique ID, bank details, stamp paper, etc.). 6. Application scrutiny by KSUM officials. 7. Shortlisting based on eligibility and proposal quality. 8. Pitch before the Expert Committee (varies by scheme). 9. Selection based on evaluation criteria (team, product innovation, marketing, financials, fund utilization plan). 10. Execute agreement with KSUM. 11. Fund disbursement in installments based on milestone completion and utilization certificate submission.
required_documents: Rs.200 worth Stamp paper in the name of the company
CA certified No Dues Certificate (for certain grants)
Revenue generation documents (for Market Acceleration/Scale-up Grant)
Balance sheet for last two years (for Scale-up Grant)
Project plan with milestones and time frame
Progress report and utilisation certificate for subsequent tranches
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted year-round with periodic calls for proposals published through official channels.
implementing_agency: Kerala Startup Mission (KSUM), a nodal agency of the Government of Kerala under the Electronics and IT Department

caveats: Grants are not generally given for service startups and SMEs working in trade and commerce
Startups must not have any other pending dues with government agencies, KSUM, or other incubators
Founder salaries, purchase of fixed assets (land, building, high-end equipment, costly software above ₹2 lakhs), rent, and major infrastructure setup are not permitted under most grants
KSUM Unique ID is mandatory for fund disbursement (though not always for application)
Company incorporation and active MCA status are required before fund release
Preference is given to startups that have not availed funding from any Government of India/State Govt. body
Shareholding by Indian promoters must be at least 51%
Some grants (e.g., NIDHI Prayas) require physical product development; pure software projects are not eligible
Women/transgender-focused schemes require ≥51% shareholding by women/transgender founders
